meaning.name: Choose NovaLife
meaning.purpose: A visitor who has heard of NovaLife finds out what it is, what each service covers and costs, who works there and how to become a patient, and goes on to book.

They choose a service, and read what it covers, who it is for, and its appointment types with their prices, which patients pay themselves. SC2, R2, R7 3. They read how NovaLife differs from the traditional approach, and its vision with its limit. SC3, R3, R4 4. They see the clinicians who work there. SC4, R8 5. They read how to become a patient, what happens at the first visit and what to bring. SC5, R9 6. They find the hours, the address and the phone. SC6, R5 7. meaning.name: Book an appointment
meaning.purpose: A visitor books an appointment type with a doctor at a free time, signing in or creating an account on the way, and has it confirmed on the next screen.
meaning.steps: 1. The visitor chooses an appointment type and sees its price; booking asks for no medical details, and says it is not for emergencies. SC8, R6, R7, R11 2. They choose a doctor who gives the type, or any, and a day; booking shows the free times, or, with none that day, the nearest days that have one. SC8, R14, R6 3. They choose a time and Continue; Continue with no time asks for one. SC8, R6 4. Signed out, they sign in, and the time is kept. SC9, R16, R6 5. New to NovaLife, they create an account with their name, date of birth, email, phone and a password, and the time is kept. SC21, R16, R6 6. They check the type, the doctor, the time and the price, which they pay themselves at the visit, and book. SC10, R6, R7 7. If the time was just booked by someone else, nothing is booked, and the nearest free times show. SC10, R6 8. If the booking fails, nothing is booked, what was chosen is kept, and they try again. SC10, R6 9. The next screen confirms it: the type, the doctor, the day and the time. SC11, R6

meaning.name: Cancel a booking
meaning.purpose: A patient cancels a booking to come, online up to 24 hours before it starts, or by phoning the clinic after that, and its time is free for others again.
meaning.steps: 1. The patient opens My bookings and sees those to come and those past. SC12, R17 2. They choose Cancel on a booking to come, and confirm it. SC12, R15 3. Less than 24 hours before, the website refuses, and gives the clinic's phone. SC12, R15 5. They phone the clinic. This step is outside the website. 6. They write the caller's first and last name, date of birth and phone, and their email where they have one; with no phone, the website refuses. SC15, R6 4. They choose the type, the doctor and a free time, as in booking. SC15, R6, R14 5. They book: it is made in the caller's name, as if the caller had booked it, and recorded as made by the staff for them. SC15, R6 6. They set the hours of each day they see patients, and save; booking offers each slot of those hours less those booked. SC16, R14 4. They add a day away; booking offers none of their times that day. SC16, R14 5. If they have bookings that day, the website names them, and saves the day only once each is cancelled. SC16, R14 6. meaning.question: Which privacy law applies to what booking keeps, in New York, and what does it require of booking and of the privacy notice (R6, R10)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: HIPAA binds a provider that sends claims or other standard transactions electronically, so a clinic paid only by its patients may fall outside it unless it does so for anything, e-prescribing or a laboratory included; New York's SHIELD Act asks for reasonable security of the private information it keeps and notice of a breach, and was read as covering medical information since 2025; a New York health information privacy act was vetoed in December 2025 and a revised bill was pending in 2026; tracking scripts on a booking page are where federal guidance has been strictest.
meaning.why: booking takes a person's details for a medical appointment, and the law decides how they are kept, which tools the website may use on the booking pages, and what the notice must say

meaning.question: Which rules on health advertising apply to what the website says about the services and about longevity (R2, R4)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: New York's Education Law 6530(27) and the Regents' rule 8 NYCRR 29.1 forbid a physician's advertising that is false or misleading, guarantees a result, or claims what cannot be substantiated, allow a patient's testimonial only with their written consent and the rule's conditions, and ask that a copy of each advertisement be kept for a year after it last appears; the FTC asks that a health claim rest on competent and reliable scientific evidence.
meaning.why: a claim the rules do not allow puts the clinic at risk, the longevity wording is where one is likeliest, and the staff change the words themselves (R13), so the rules may also decide who approves a change and what is kept of it

meaning.question: Which rules on prices apply to patients who pay themselves, and what must the website show to meet them (R6, R7)? Background read on 2026-10-20, for the adviser to confirm, not settled: under the federal No Surprises Act a provider tells a patient who pays themselves that a good faith estimate of the cost is available -- in a notice on its website, in the office and when a visit is scheduled -- and gives one when a visit is booked some days ahead or when asked; CMS publishes a model notice.
meaning.why: R7 shows a price per appointment type, and these rules may ask for a notice on the website and an estimate with each booking, which would change booking (R6) and the confirmation

meaning.question: FD10 says every control is at least 44 pixels high; FD3 says 44 for a button or a field, 40 for a free time and 32 for a small button; and the links of the header and the footer are drawn 24 high. Which holds?
meaning.why: It decides how every link, free time and small button is built, and whether the prototypes change.

meaning.name: The home page presents NovaLife
meaning.statement: When anyone opens the website's home page, the website shall show the clinic's name, its tagline, its mission and its central idea, with a way from there to each of the four services and to booking.

meaning.says: Given the home page, when it opens, then it shows "NovaLife Clinic", "The Future of Health" and the mission "Help people understand their health, act earlier, and stay healthier for longer."
Given the home page, when it opens, then it shows the central idea "Don't just treat illness. Help people protect their health today and preserve it for the future."
Given the home page, when one of the four services is chosen on it, then that service's page opens (R2).
Given the home page, when booking is chosen on it, then booking opens (R6).

meaning.name: Privacy
meaning.statement: The website shall show, on a page reached from every page and from booking, what it keeps about a visitor, why, who reads it and for how long.

meaning.says: Given any page, when Privacy is chosen, then the privacy notice opens.
Given booking, when it opens, then it leads to the privacy notice before anything is booked.
Given the privacy notice, when it opens, then it says what a booking keeps, why, who reads it and for how long.

meaning.name: Not for emergencies
meaning.statement: The website shall say, on every page and on booking, that it is not for medical emergencies, and give the emergency number to call instead.

meaning.says: Given any page, when it opens, then it says that the website is not for medical emergencies, and to call 911 in one.
Given booking, when it opens, then it says, above the form, that a booked appointment is not emergency care and that an emergency is a call to that number.

meaning.name: Staff sign in
meaning.statement: When a member of staff signs in with their email and password, the website shall open the staff area to them.

meaning.says: Given a member of staff with an account, when they sign in with their email and password, then the staff area opens.
Given a wrong password, or an email with no account, when someone signs in, then sign-in is refused with one message that does not say which of the two was wrong.
Given someone not signed in, when they open an address of the staff area, then sign-in opens in its place.
Given a signed-in member of staff, when they sign out, then the staff area closes, and its addresses ask for sign-in again.

Given a member of staff who has forgotten their password, when they ask to reset it on staff sign-in, then the website sends a link to their email that lets them set a new one, and says the same whether or not the email has a staff account.

meaning.name: Staff change what the website says
meaning.statement: The website shall let a signed-in administrator change the text and pictures of every page, the services and their appointment types, the opening hours, the prices and the team, and show each change to visitors once it is saved.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in administrator, when they change a service's description and save, then the service's page shows the new description.
Given a signed-in administrator, when they change an appointment type's price and save, then its service's page and booking show the new price (R7).
Given a signed-in administrator, when they add an appointment type with its service, its length, its price and the doctors who give it, and save, then booking offers it with those doctors (R6).
Given a signed-in administrator, when they add a clinician with a name, a photograph, a role and qualifications and save, then the Team page shows them (R8).
Given a signed-in administrator, when they change the opening hours and save, then the Contact page shows the new hours (R5).
Given a change that is not saved, when the administrator leaves the page, then the website warns that the change will be lost.
Given a change that fails to be saved, when the administrator saves, then the website says so, keeps the change written, and visitors still see what was there before.

meaning.name: Staff set each doctor's free times
meaning.statement: The website shall let the staff set the days and hours each doctor sees patients -- an administrator or the front desk for any doctor, a doctor for themselves (R18) -- and offer in booking only those hours that are not yet booked.

meaning.says: Given a doctor set to see patients on Mondays from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM, when a visitor books a 30-minute appointment type with that doctor, then booking offers every half hour from 9:00 to 12:30 on Mondays, less the times already booked, one appointment starting as the one before it ends (R6).
Given a doctor marked away on December 24, when a visitor books with that doctor, then booking offers no time on December 24.
Given a day on which a doctor already has bookings, when the doctor is marked away that day, then the website names those bookings, and saves the change only once each is moved or cancelled.

meaning.name: Cancel a booking
meaning.statement: When a patient cancels their booking at least 24 hours before it starts, the website shall cancel it and offer its time in booking again.

meaning.says: Given a booking on November 20 at 10:00 AM, when its patient cancels it on November 19 at 9:00 AM, then it shows as cancelled, and 10:00 AM on November 20 is free again in booking.

Given a booking on November 20 at 10:00 AM, when its patient tries to cancel it on November 19 at 11:00 AM, then the website refuses, says that a booking less than 24 hours away is cancelled by phoning the clinic, and gives the clinic's phone number.
Given a person who phones to cancel their booking, when the staff member who answers cancels it on the website, then it is cancelled and its time is free again, however close to its start.
Given a patient who wants another time, when they look at their booking, then the website offers to cancel it and book again; it does not move a booking.
Given a patient signed in, when they look for another patient's booking, then they cannot see it or cancel it (R17).

meaning.name: Patient account
meaning.statement: When a visitor creates an account with their first and last name, date of birth, email, phone and a password, the website shall open the account and book with its details from then on.

meaning.says: Given a visitor with no account, when they give their first and last name, date of birth, email, phone and a password and create the account, then it opens, and booking fills in their details.
Given an email that already has an account, when a visitor creates an account with it, then the website refuses, says that the email has an account, and offers to sign in or to reset the password.
Given a detail missing, or a date of birth in the future, when a visitor creates the account, then the website refuses and says which detail and why, keeping everything else written.
Given a patient with an account, when they sign in with their email and password, then their account opens.
Given a wrong password, or an email with no account, when someone signs in, then sign-in is refused with one message that does not say which of the two was wrong.
Given a patient who has forgotten their password, when they ask to reset it, then the website sends a link to their email that lets them set a new one.

meaning.name: My bookings
meaning.statement: While a patient is signed in, the website shall show them their bookings, those to come and those past, and let them cancel one from there (R15).

meaning.says: Given a signed-in patient with a booking on November 20 and one on October 2, when they open My bookings on October 17, then November 20 shows under those to come and October 2 under those past.
Given a signed-in patient with no booking, when they open My bookings, then it says they have none, and offers booking.
Given a booking to come, when the patient cancels it from My bookings, then it is cancelled as R15 says.
Given another patient's booking, when this patient is signed in, then it never shows to them.

meaning.name: Staff roles
meaning.statement: The website shall let each member of staff do only what their role allows: an administrator everything in the staff area; the front desk booking and cancelling for callers and setting any doctor's free times; a doctor setting their own free times and days away.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in administrator, when they open the staff area, then they can change the pages, the services and their appointment types, the prices, the team, the opening hours, every doctor's free times and the staff accounts.
Given a signed-in member of the front desk, when they book or cancel for a caller, or set a doctor's free times, then the website does it.
Given a signed-in member of the front desk, when they try to change a page, a price, an appointment type or a staff account, then the website refuses and says that only an administrator can.
Given a signed-in doctor, when they set their own free times or mark themselves away, then the website does it (R14).
Given a signed-in doctor, when they try to change another doctor's free times, a page, a price or a booking, then the website refuses.

meaning.name: Staff accounts
meaning.statement: When an administrator adds a member of staff with their name, email and role, the website shall create their account and send them a link to set their password.

meaning.says: Given a signed-in administrator, when they add Dr. Lee with her email and the role doctor, then Dr. Lee receives a link by email, sets her password with it, and signs in as a doctor (R12).
Given an email that already has a staff account, when an administrator adds it again, then the website refuses and says so.
Given a member of staff an administrator has removed, when they try to sign in, then sign-in is refused.
Given one administrator left, when an administrator tries to remove that account or change its role, then the website refuses, so that the staff area always has an administrator.
Given the website on the day it launches, when it is first opened, then one administrator account exists, set up at launch, and no other.

meaning.name: A page for each of the four services
meaning.statement: The website shall give each of NovaLife's four services -- general medical care; prevention and early detection; longevity and healthy aging; high-tech, personalized healthcare -- a page of its own that says what the service covers, who it is for and how to start it.

meaning.says: Given the general medical care page, when it opens, then it names consultations, medical assessments, diagnosis, treatment, referrals and follow-up by qualified healthcare professionals.
Given the prevention and early detection page, when it opens, then it names screening, check-ups, diagnostic tests and regular health reviews.
Given the longevity and healthy aging page, when it opens, then it names maintaining physical and cognitive health, reducing preventable risks and supporting healthy aging over the long term.

Given the high-tech, personalized healthcare page, when it opens, then it names digital health records, longitudinal health data, AI-assisted workflows and monitoring tools, and says that technology supports the clinicians and does not replace their judgment.
Given any of the four pages, when it opens, then it says who the service is for, and offers booking with that service's appointment types (R6).

meaning.name: How NovaLife is different
meaning.statement: The website shall show how NovaLife differs from the traditional approach, point by point: proactive and preventive rather than reactive; a connected view of health rather than separate appointments and results; personalized, evidence-based plans rather than general recommendations; long-term wellbeing rather than the current illness alone; a digital-first experience rather than paper-based or fragmented processes.

meaning.says: Given the page on what makes NovaLife different, when it opens, then it shows the five comparisons, each as the traditional approach beside NovaLife's.
Given the same page, when it opens, then it says "Technology supports medical professionals; it does not replace their judgment."

meaning.name: The vision and the ambition, with their limit
meaning.statement: The website shall present NovaLife's vision and its long-term ambition of healthy longevity, and say wherever it does so that immortality is an aspirational idea, not a current medical capability or a promise the clinic makes.

meaning.says: Given the About page, when it opens, then it shows the vision "The Future of Health", the mission, and the ambition to push the boundaries of healthy human longevity through evidence-based prevention, early detection and better management of established health risks.
Given any page that speaks of longevity or of the ambition, when it opens, then it says that immortality is an aspirational idea, not a current medical capability or a promise the clinic makes.
Given any page of the website, when it is read, then no sentence on it promises a longer life, a cure or a result of care.

meaning.name: Opening hours, address and how to reach the clinic
meaning.statement: The website shall show the clinic's opening hours, its address, how to get there, its phone number and its email on a Contact page reached from every page.

meaning.says: Given any page, when Contact is chosen, then the Contact page opens.

Given the Contact page, when it opens, then it shows the hours of each day of the week, the address with a map of where it is, how to get there, the phone with the hours it is answered, and the email.
Given the clinic's hours have changed, when the Contact page opens, then it shows the new hours.

meaning.name: Book an appointment online
meaning.statement: When a signed-in patient chooses an appointment type and a doctor's free time, the website shall book that time and confirm the booking on the next screen.

meaning.says: Given a doctor free on 20 November at 10:00, when a signed-in patient chooses an appointment type that doctor gives, that doctor and that time, and books, then the next screen confirms the booking with the appointment type, the doctor, the day and the time, and 10:00 that day is no longer free.
Given a time another visitor booked while this one was booking, when this one books it, then the website says the time was just taken, books nothing, and shows the nearest free times.
Given a booking that fails to be made, when the visitor books, then the website says so, books nothing, keeps what was written, and offers to try again.
Given booking, when it opens, then it asks for no medical details, and says that symptoms and results are discussed with the doctor, not written in the form.

Given a person who phones the clinic, when the staff member who answers books on the website with that person's first and last name, date of birth and phone, and their email where they have one, then the booking is made in that person's name, as if they had booked it themselves, and is recorded as made by the staff for them.
Given a caller with no email, when the staff book for them with a phone alone, then the booking is made without an account, and the caller cancels it by phoning (R15).
Given a caller with no phone, when the staff try to book for them, then the website refuses and says that a phone number is always needed.
Given the staff booking for a caller, when the form opens, then it marks the phone as required and the email as wanted but not required.
Given a visitor who is not signed in, when they choose a time and book, then the website asks them to sign in or create an account (R16), keeps the time chosen, and books it once they have.
Given an appointment type, when it is chosen in booking, then booking shows only the doctors who give it and only their free times.
Given any appointment type, when a visitor books it, then nothing is asked of them first: no earlier consultation is needed for any type.
Given a day on which no doctor giving the chosen appointment type is free, when the visitor chooses it, then the website says so and shows the nearest days with a free time.

meaning.name: The price of each appointment type
meaning.statement: The website shall show the price of each appointment type on its service's page and in booking before anything is booked.

meaning.says: Given a service's page, when it opens, then it shows each of the service's appointment types with its price in US dollars.
Given booking, when an appointment type is chosen, then its price shows before the visitor books.
Given an appointment type's price has changed, when its service's page or booking opens, then the new price shows.
Given any service's page, when it opens, then it says that patients pay the clinic themselves, and that the clinic does not bill health insurance.

meaning.name: The team
meaning.statement: The website shall show the clinicians who work at NovaLife, each with their name, role and qualifications.

meaning.says: Given the Team page, when it opens, then each clinician shows with their name, photograph, role and qualifications.
Given a clinician who has left the clinic, when the Team page opens, then they are not on it.

meaning.name: Before becoming a patient
meaning.statement: The website shall answer, on one page, how to become a patient, what happens at the first visit, and what to bring to it.

meaning.says: Given the page for new patients, when it opens, then it answers how to become a patient, what happens at the first visit, and what to bring to it.
Given an answer on that page that concerns a service, when it is read, then it leads to that service's page (R2).

meaning.name: NovaLife Clinic website
meaning.non-goals: - A patient portal: a patient's account holds their details and their bookings, and nothing of their care -- health records, results, monitoring data and messages with a clinician belong to the clinic's care, not to this website. - Medical advice: the website informs and does not assess symptoms or recommend care, because technology supports the clinicians and does not replace their judgment. - Paying online: the website takes no payment. - A second way to book, for the clinic's staff: a person who phones is booked by the staff on the website itself, so that every booking is made in one place.
meaning.problem: NovaLife Clinic is a general medical clinic built around prevention, personalized care and healthy longevity, which its concept sets against the traditional, reactive approach. Without a place that says what it offers, how it differs and how to become a patient, the people it is for cannot find out, and cannot choose it. The clinic is not open yet: the website opens with it, so it is how people first learn of NovaLife, and nobody can find out about it or reach it any other way today, 2026-10-20.
meaning.summary: NovaLife Clinic's website presents the clinic -- its vision, its four services and how it differs from a traditional practice -- to the people who might become its patients. It gives them, in one place, every practical thing they need to choose the clinic and to get in touch with it. It is the clinic's marketing and its front door.
meaning.users: The visitor: someone considering NovaLife for their own health -- for general care, for a check-up or screening, or for healthy aging -- who has not yet been in touch with the clinic. The patient: someone with an account, who signs in to book, to see their bookings and to cancel one, and comes back for the hours, the address or how to reach the clinic. The clinic: NovaLife's staff, who sign in to the staff area in one of three roles -- the administrator, who keeps everything the website shows current and the staff accounts; the front desk, who books and cancels on the website for a person who phones and sets the doctors' free times; and the doctors, who set their own.
